name: Capacitor-Grade BOPP/Dielectric Films
scope: Ultra-thin metallised BOPP/PET dielectric film for film capacitors (EV inverters and chargers, solar/wind inverters, grid capacitor banks, drives) and the Indian listed companies making, metallising, buying or adjacent to it.

summary.one_line: A quiet week for capacitor film itself. Cosmo First's GST search ended with no material impact, while Jindal Poly's 12-day JPFL standstill ran to about 25 Nov with no extension or settlement disclosed. All four producers except SRF fell 4-7% over the week.
key_points: Cosmo First: the Maharashtra GST search at its Aurangabad units, which began on 18 Nov, concluded on 24 Nov. The company says it had no material impact (S12). There is still no new capacitor-film disclosure, and its website still calls the second metalliser forthcoming (S3).

Jindal Poly: the 13 Nov standstill with JPFL Films and Brookfield-affiliated Project Holdings Fourteen covered 12 days. Proceedings can resume unless the standstill is extended or a settlement is reached (S23). The company's latest filing on Screener, as of the 25 Nov close, is a 16 Nov newspaper publication. No extension or settlement had been disclosed (S13).

Xpro India says it meets about one-third of India's dielectric BOPP demand, with most of the rest imported (S26). In Q2 FY27 its dielectric revenue rose 64% YoY, and some key customers have approved its 3.5-micron film (S25). The Rs 370 cr postal ballot for its UAE subsidiary is still open; no result was listed by 25 Nov (S16).

Jindal Poly, Q2 FY27 (unchanged): revenue was Rs 738 cr (+26.5% YoY) with a consolidated net loss of about Rs 85-86 cr (S18, S22). The review is qualified over unverified inventory at the fire-hit subsidiary (S18).
ECMS: the 6 Nov round includes polypropylene film among its products. The applicant is still unnamed, and we found no newer round. The cumulative total is 118 approvals and Rs 77,051 cr (S24).

Market size (unchanged): QYResearch puts global capacitor-grade BOPP at USD 874.5 mn in 2025, reaching USD 1,336.2 mn by 2032 (6.25% CAGR) (S17). IndexBox sees 6-9% annual growth over 2026-35, with EV power electronics at 10-14% (S1).
Prices, 18 to 25 Nov 2026: Xpro fell 6.9% to 78x P/E, Cosmo fell 4.5% and Jindal Poly fell 4.2%, while SRF rose 2.9%. All four are 20-38% below their 52-week highs (S12, S13, S14, S16).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Xpro India has the most direct exposure. Dielectric film made up Rs 135.52 cr of FY26 sales (S15), and dielectric revenue grew 64% YoY in Q2 FY27 (S25). Xpro says it supplies about a third of Indian demand, and imports supply most of the rest, which leaves room for import substitution (S26). The stock is still at 78x P/E after this week's dip (S16).
Domestic metallisers and capacitor makers, including ECMS approvals and the unnamed polypropylene-film applicant from the 6 Nov round, add demand for local base film (S10, S24).
SRF has run a capacitor-grade BOPP plant at Indore since 15 May 2026, built for about Rs 277 cr (S9). The business is small within the group's Rs 18,265 cr of sales (S14).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Jindal Poly: Q2 swung to a loss with a qualified consolidated review (S18). The JPFL standstill period has ended and no extension or settlement has been disclosed (S13, S23). The SEBI show-cause notice is still open (S6), and the latest CRISIL rationale we opened has the ratings on Watch Negative (S7).
Qualification is slow. Xpro's approvals turn into volume only after 1,000-2,000 hour life tests (S25).

Domestic capacity is rising at SRF, Xpro (Barjora plus UAE), JPFL (5,000 TPA per CRISIL) and the ECMS polypropylene-film project (S7, S9, S24, S25). No source we could verify quantifies Indian demand in tonnes.
Polypropylene accounts for 50-65% of production cost, and China holds 35-45% of global capacity (S1).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Jindal Poly: whether the standstill is extended or settled, or whether NCLT and arbitration proceedings resume (S23).
Xpro: the postal-ballot result for the UAE-subsidiary transactions, the UAE line's commercial start later in FY27, and further approvals of its ultra-thin grades (S16, S25).
The name of the 6 Nov ECMS polypropylene-film applicant (S24).
Cosmo: start-up of the second metalliser (S3).
Finance Ministry notification of DGTR's PET-film anti-dumping recommendation; the case does not cover BOPP (S8).

blocks.text: Capacitor-grade film is an ultra-thin dielectric film, the insulating layer between a capacitor's plates. It is mostly biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP), vacuum-metallised with aluminium or aluminium-zinc and wound into film capacitors. Cosmo First makes it at 2.5-12 micron, in clean-room conditions with micro-slitting, for AC and DC capacitors (S2). Xpro India makes 2-16 micron base film for power capacitors, EV systems and railways (S15). Packaging BOPP is thicker and has no comparable purity or surface requirements. The thin metal layer lets the capacitor 'self-heal': a local short burns the metal away instead of destroying the part.

Demand is moving to thinner films with higher breakdown voltage. IndexBox sees EV demand shifting to 2-4 micron BOPP. It expects BOPP to keep 60-70% of volume, with metallised film at 40-50% of value (S1). Prices rise steeply as films get thinner. Xpro's indicative prices, from its 9 Nov investor meet (S25):

items: Conventional film: about Rs 470-480/kg.
3.5 micron: slightly above Rs 600/kg.
3 micron: possibly close to Rs 900/kg.

blocks.text: Cosmo's metallised grades show the range of end uses (S3):

items: Al-Zn standard: fans and motor-run capacitors.
Slope/RMF: APFC panels and wind.
Segmented: power supplies.
'Series': variable-frequency drives, renewable inverters, UPS and EVs.

blocks.text: Xpro also names EV inverters, solar and wind, grid equipment, railways and data centres as end markets (S25).

blocks.caption: Third-party forecasts (each is the publisher's own forecast)

blocks.title: Global capacitor-grade BOPP film market (QYResearch forecast)

blocks.text: Both forecasts point to mid-to-high single-digit growth. QYResearch names Xpro India and the B.C. Jindal group among global suppliers, alongside Toray, Oji, Shin-Etsu, Bolloré, Tervakoski and Chinese producers (S17). We did not verify the Mordor and FMI figures, so they are left out. We found no verified figure for the size of the Indian market.

When Cosmo launched capacitor film in Dec 2023, it said India largely imported the product from China, and saw room for import substitution and exports (S2). Xpro now says it meets about one-third of domestic dielectric BOPP demand and that most of the rest is imported (S26). China holds 35-45% of global capacity (S1). We found no official tonnage series for India's capacitor-film imports.

DGTR has recommended anti-dumping duties on PET film from Bangladesh, China and Thailand (S8). As of 26 Nov we found no Finance Ministry notification. The case covers PET film, not BOPP, the main capacitor dielectric (S1). We found no trade action specific to capacitor BOPP.

subsections.title: Confirmed producers: what changed this week

blocks.text: Cosmo First disclosed on 25 Nov that the Maharashtra GST search at its Aurangabad units, which began on 18 Nov, concluded on 24 Nov. The company says it had no material impact (S12). That removes last week's overhang. There is still no capacitor-film disclosure: the Q2 FY27 release covers specialty chemicals, coated films and Plastech, and does not mention capacitor film (S19).

Jindal Poly Films: the 13 Nov standstill paused all pending proceedings for 12 days, to explore an amicable resolution. No money changes hands under it, and the proceedings can resume when it ends unless it is extended or the parties settle (S23). As of the 25 Nov close, the latest filing on Screener was a 16 Nov newspaper publication. No extension or settlement had been disclosed (S13). The Q2 FY27 results still frame the stock (S18, S22):

items: Revenue was Rs 738.1 cr, up 26.5% YoY (S18).
The consolidated net loss was Rs 85.2 cr (S18), or Rs 86.17 cr in a second summary, including a Rs 96.43 cr fair-value loss on investments (S22).
The consolidated review is qualified: the auditor could not verify inventory at the subsidiary hit by the May 2025 Nashik fire (S18). That inventory is carried at Rs 277.74 cr (S22).
The standalone loss of Rs 350 cr includes a Rs 292 cr provision against a loan to a subsidiary (S18).

blocks.text: Xpro India: no new filing after the 14 Nov postal-ballot advertisement (S16). The resolutions seek approval for Rs 370 cr of transactions with the UAE subsidiary, including a Rs 220 cr guarantee and a Rs 60 cr loan (S16). On its 9 Nov call, management said dielectric revenue rose 64% YoY and dielectric exports nearly doubled. Some key customers have approved the 3.5-micron film, while others are still running 1,000-2,000 hour life tests (S25). Xpro also exports dielectric and specialty films to North America and Europe (S26).

SRF: the Indore capacitor-grade BOPP plant has been running since 15 May 2026 (S9). Its 14-20 Nov filings are SAST disclosures and a small customs penalty order, none of them about capacitor film (S14).

Only Xpro India reports capacitor-film revenue: Rs 135.52 cr on 3,541 MT in FY26 (S15), plus the Q2 growth rate (S25). Any capacitor-film share for SRF, Cosmo or Jindal Poly would be an estimate, so none is given.

items: Pan Electronics (India), BSE 517397: a Bengaluru micro-cap that has metallised polypropylene and polyester dielectric films since 1986 and has moved into MPP capacitors (S11). It is immaterial in size.
Universal Cables makes all-polypropylene LT/HT power capacitors and APFC panels, so it is a potential domestic film buyer (S5). No film-supply tie-up has been disclosed.
Polyplex and UFlex (Flex Films): IndexBox lists both among Indian dielectric-film producers (S1), but we found no company-confirmed capacitor grade. Both stay in 'other'.

blocks.text: Coverage gap: India's main film-capacitor makers (e.g. TDK India, Vishay India) are unlisted subsidiaries, and the 6 Nov ECMS polypropylene-film applicant is unnamed (S24). The listed exposure is therefore three small caps (Xpro, Cosmo and Jindal Poly), a micro-cap metalliser (Pan Electronics) and a large cap where capacitor film is a small business (SRF). We found no mid-cap pure play.

blocks.title: Share price change, 18 Nov to 25 Nov 2026

blocks.text: Xpro gave back about half of the prior fortnight's 14% gain but still trades at 78x trailing P/E (S16). Despite the dip, it remains the only name the market values for dielectric film. Cosmo is at 9.3x (S12), so the market gives little value to its capacitor line. Jindal Poly trades at about 0.90x book, given its loss and the unresolved JPFL dispute (S13). SRF is valued as a large-cap chemicals business (S14). All four are 20-38% below their 52-week highs (S12, S13, S14, S16). We could not confirm 6- and 12-month returns from a source we opened, so they are left out.

Coverage remains thin. Most of what exists comes from aggregators summarising filings and calls (S20, S25, S26), and Jindal Poly's coverage focuses on the dispute and losses, not capacitor film (S18, S22). We found no Indian broker note or mainstream-media piece built around capacitor film.

items: Resin cost: polypropylene accounts for 50-65% of production cost (S1).
Chinese overcapacity: China holds 35-45% of global capacity (S1), and imports still supply most Indian demand beyond Xpro's share (S2, S26).
Qualification lag: Xpro's volumes follow only after 1,000-2,000 hour life tests (S25).
Execution at Xpro's UAE plant: management flags the regional conflict as a risk, and the plant needs Rs 370 cr of parent support (S16, S25).
Domestic supply build-out: SRF (S9), Xpro (S25), JPFL at 5,000 TPA (S7) and the ECMS polypropylene-film approval (S24). We found no verified figure for Indian demand in tonnes.
Small share of revenue: capacitor film does not feature among the reported drivers at Cosmo or SRF (S14, S19).

Governance at Jindal Poly: a qualified consolidated review and a Rs 292 cr loan provision (S18), a JPFL dispute whose standstill period has run out (S23), the open SEBI notice (S6) and CRISIL's Watch Negative (S7).
Settlement, extension or resumption of the JPFL proceedings (S23); confirmation of JPFL's capacitor-film doubling (S4, S7).
Xpro's postal-ballot result, the UAE line's commercial start and further approvals of its ultra-thin grades (S16, S25).
Naming of the 6 Nov ECMS polypropylene-film applicant, and any further ECMS rounds (S24).
Cosmo's second metalliser coming on stream (S3).
Localisation of EV and solar inverters, the segment IndexBox expects to grow 10-14% a year (S1).
Notification of the PET-film anti-dumping duty (S8). We found no trade action specific to capacitor BOPP.

companies.name: Xpro India Ltd
companies.role: Dedicated BOPP dielectric base-film maker at Barjora (2-16 micron). FY26 dielectric sales were Rs 135.52 cr on 3,541 MT (S15). India capacity is 8,000 MT/yr after the Barjora line, with a third line coming in the UAE (S25). Claims about one-third of Indian demand (S26).
companies.impact: Dielectric revenue rose 64% YoY in Q2, and some key customers have approved its 3.5-micron grade (S25). At 78x P/E (S16), execution on the UAE line and approvals from life tests have to keep pace.

companies.name: SRF Ltd
companies.role: Commissioned phase 1 of its Indore capacitor-grade BOPP plant on 15 May 2026, at about Rs 277 cr (S9). Holds an ECMS approval for a Rs 496 cr capacitor PP-film project (S10).
companies.impact: A scaling domestic competitor to Xpro and Cosmo, but small within the group's Rs 18,265 cr of sales (S14).

companies.name: Cosmo First Ltd
companies.role: Makes metallised capacitor-grade BOPP, launched in Dec 2023 at ~750 MT/yr in 2.5-12 micron (S2). The metalliser is now rated 900 MT/yr, with a second forthcoming (S3).
companies.impact: The GST search ended on 24 Nov with no material impact, per the company (S12). Capacitor film does not feature in Q2 FY27 drivers (S19). Trades at 9.3x P/E (S12).

companies.name: Jindal Poly Films Ltd
companies.role: Its subsidiary JPFL Films makes capacitor film. CRISIL says 5,000 TPA is operational (S7), and a Rs 250 cr doubling was announced in 2024 (S4). QYResearch lists the B.C. Jindal group among global players (S17).
companies.impact: Q2 FY27 loss of about Rs 85 cr with a qualified consolidated review (S18). The 12-day JPFL standstill ran out with no extension or settlement disclosed (S13, S23), and the SEBI notice is still open (S6). Governance outweighs the capacitor theme.

companies.name: Pan Electronics (India) Ltd
companies.role: Bengaluru micro-cap that metallises polypropylene and polyester dielectric films (since 1986) and now makes MPP capacitors (S11).
companies.impact: A potential buyer of domestic base film, but immaterial in investment terms given its tiny size (S11).

companies.name: Universal Cables Ltd
companies.role: Makes all-polypropylene LT/HT power capacitors and APFC panels (S5).
companies.impact: A potential domestic film buyer as local supply grows; no film-supply tie-up has been disclosed (S5).

companies.role: BOPET film maker that IndexBox lists among Indian dielectric-film producers (S1).
companies.impact: Adjacent only: no company-confirmed capacitor grade. The PET-film anti-dumping case matters more to it (S8).

method:
Weekly refresh of the 2026-W47 edition (19 Nov), researched on 26 Nov 2026 with web search and page fetches.

New this edition:
- Cosmo First's 25 Nov disclosure that the GST search concluded on 24 Nov with no material impact, from the Screener announcements list (S12). A SAHI news item seen in search covered only the start of the search.
- Xpro's claim to meet about one-third of Indian dielectric BOPP demand, from a 5 Nov summary of its investor presentation (S26).
- Prices and valuations: Screener closes for 25 Nov, fetched 26 Nov. Changes are measured against the 18 Nov closes in the W47 edition. The dashboard's numbers.json snapshot was taken earlier on 25 Nov, so it may differ slightly.

Checked but not found:
- Any extension, settlement or follow-up filing on the JPFL standstill (searches, NSE archive results and Screener's announcements list; the latest filing is dated 16 Nov).
- Xpro's postal-ballot result.
- A new ECMS round, or the name of the 6 Nov polypropylene-film applicant.
- A Finance Ministry notification of the PET anti-dumping duty; an e-gazette PDF surfaced in search but could not be opened.
- A CRISIL rationale after May 2026; Screener lists a 12 Nov CRISIL update, but its content was not seen.
- Any Indian broker or mainstream-media capacitor-film thematic piece.

Dropped:
- The Whalesbook NCLT article (old S21), so the numbering skips S21.
- Last week's GST-search overhang for Cosmo, now resolved.

Carried over without re-opening: IndexBox, QYResearch, the May 2026 CRISIL rationale, the PET anti-dumping article, the company profile pages and the Q2 result summaries.

Not stated because not confirmed: capacitor-film revenue for SRF, Cosmo or Jindal Poly, Indian import tonnage or market size, and 6- and 12-month returns.

No ratings or price targets are given.
